order: Apply a second class-boundary redraw scoped strictly to the three findings in the prior disagreement ledger. Recast one discriminator on where the evidence lives — evidence existing only during a live run, nothing persisted, routes one way, while evidence persisting in a readable artifact routes the other, and a symptom merely being active or recurring is never by itself sufficient — and mirror the wording in the phase-chain rule and the related discriminator. Add a new discriminator closing the gap between the two ambiguous classes, keyed on whether content was recovered by reconciling a corpus versus settled at intake. Give one discriminator an explicit unit definition, and add a preamble rule scoping each discriminator to its own two classes. Resolve the three flagged items and log any previously agreed item that shifts under the tightened rule. Leave validation of this redraw an open decision for the owner before the downstream work order proceeds.
claims: All three flagged items resolved determinately under the redrawn boundary, and one previously agreed item was found to shift under the tightened unit rule and was logged openly rather than silently changed. No class pair reached the three-entry merge trigger. The redraw was scoped to exactly the three findings, with two options for validating it recorded as an open decision for the owner, and the downstream work order stays gated until that decision is made.
